title: Home page Lights tab: pick a card style (round 2b)

steps.headline: Which card style should each room use on the Lights tab?
steps.notice: Each room is one card with the page's own round All button, the palette scenes button, the fold arrow and the room bar on top. Cards start closed; here Destin's Room is open, with its unreachable TV backlight last.
steps.risk: All three keep your earlier choices; colour pop-ups close on an outside click or Escape.

variants.label: Roomy rows
variants.summary: One wide, roomy row per light: bulb, name and percent on top, a thick bar underneath, and a colour dot. The dot opens the colour menu inside the card, pushing the lights below it down.
variants.risk: Longest card: three working lights already fill a screen, and opening a colour menu makes it taller still. On a phone every bar stays easy to hit.

variants.label: Big tiles
variants.summary: Two or three big tiles per row. A tile glows and fills to show how bright it is, with the percent in large type. Tap to switch, drag sideways to dim. The colour dot opens a small floating colour panel next to the tile.
variants.risk: Tap and drag share one surface, so a slow, wobbly tap can dim a light instead of switching it. The floating panel covers the lights beside it until you tap away or press Escape. On a phone two tiles fit per row.

variants.label: Chips
variants.summary: Every light is one small chip you tap to switch, packed in a wrapped line so a whole room fits in a few lines. Press the little arrow on a chip and it opens into a full-width panel with its bar and a colour dot; the dot opens the floating colour panel.
variants.risk: Dimming or recolouring takes an extra press to open a chip first, and the open panel pushes the other chips down. Chips are the most compact, so names that are long get cut short on a phone.
